# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-10-23 (Fri): **The capture was reading a dead report.** The site moved to a new Power BI report around 10-05 (key `f249bea3-…`); `weekly_capture.py` still opened the old one (`6e6c66a9-…`), which still loads but froze about 10-02. So the 10-07, 10-14 and first 10-23 captures were identical copies of 10-02. `REPORT` now points at the new report (same page `fe8c0d478504c7c16beb`). Eric confirmed the site itself was current.
- 2026-10-23 re-capture with the new report: 16/16 teams, every team moved. Baylor 6.55 expected wins (raw 6-6), Kansas tomorrow 63%. Wed 10-21 was missed, but no Big 12 game was played Thu 10-22 or Fri 10-23, so the week-8 forecast is safe.
- **Lost for good:** the real pre-game forecasts for weeks 6 and 7 (games about 10-10 and 10-17). The 10-07 and 10-14 snapshots hold 10-02 numbers, so the compare grades those games against stale forecasts (week 6: 4/6 sides, week 7: 4/7). Do not count them as the model's record. Week 5 (about 10-03) is graded against the real 10-02 forecast: 4 of 7 sides correct.
- 2026-10-02 (Fri): Captured all 16 Big 12 teams. Week 4 graded: the model picked 6 of 8 unique games right. Misses: Kansas State over Cincinnati (43% Cincinnati; Cincinnati won 31-26) and West Virginia over Oklahoma State (33% Oklahoma State; Oklahoma State won 41-24, 27-pt margin miss). Baylor beat Colorado 23-13 (forecast 30-20, margin miss 0). Baylor is at 6.73 expected wins (raw 6-6), up 0.37. Model re-rated Oklahoma State and UCF up, Kansas State and West Virginia down.
- The 9/30 Wednesday capture was skipped. No forecast was lost: no games were played between 9/26 and 10/2 (no Week 5 game shows as played).
- `scripts/weekly_run.sh` now skips the comparison when the capture fails (3619c54). Before, a failed capture printed last week's comparison as if it were new.
- Playwright auto-updated and now needs browser build `chromium-1243`. It is installed on the Mac. See `docs/handoffs/2026-09-23-week3-capture.md`.
- Snapshots are in `data/weekly_snapshots/`, and copies plus comparison reports are in `../CFB_Forecast_Archive/2026/`.

## Next
1. Run the next Big 12 capture on Wednesday 2026-10-28: `scripts/weekly_run.sh` (or `/forecast-capture`). Run it headed, from the main checkout, on the Mac.
2. On 10-28, check the compare: during the season every team should move. If none move, check `REPORT` against the iframe on https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/ before blaming the site.

## Open questions
- ~~`worktree-eval-all-games`: merge or delete?~~ Deleted 2026-09-23. All five of its files were already on `main`, byte-identical. Tip was b863846.
- ~~What made Windows capture Baylor at 07:37 on 9/23?~~ Answered 2026-09-23: no capture task exists on Windows. The daily `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` popup (07:25) prompted a manual run. That task is now disabled on Windows.

## Gotchas
- `uv run --with playwright` pulls the newest playwright. When it updates, the capture dies with `Executable doesn't exist at .../chromium-<N>`. Fix: `uv run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium`, then re-run.
- **The Mac owns the weekly capture (decided 2026-09-23).** Never run it on Windows. Two machines writing the same day's snapshot and `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` conflict at the next sync.
- Run the capture from the main checkout, not a worktree. `ARCHIVE = ROOT.parent / "CFB_Forecast_Archive"` resolves to the wrong folder inside `.claude/worktrees/`, so use `--no-archive` there and copy by hand.
- A capture must run headed. A dropdown's search box renders about 1s after the click, and the script waits for it. If it fails with `search box never appeared`, the report UI changed.
- One failed attempt per team is normal; the retry recovers it.
- **"No forecast moved" in season means a dead report link, not a stale site.** The site can swap its Power BI report; the old link keeps loading frozen data with no error. Get the live link: `curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/ | grep -o 'app.powerbi.com/view?r=[^"&]*'` and compare with `REPORT` in `weekly_capture.py`. Found 2026-10-23 after three frozen captures.

- 2026-09-23: Week 3 capture; wrapper skips compare on failure (3619c54); Mac/Windows merge conflict resolved in 5bebba8.

- 2026-09-10: Captured and froze Baylor's forecast (4.49 expected wins). Auburn graded as a correct side with a 3-point margin miss.

content.text:
I captured all 16 Big 12 teams today, before Baylor plays at UCF tonight. Each team has 12 games, and the copies are in the archive.

**Missed Wednesday:** The run was due Wednesday 10-28. No Big 12 team played Thursday 10-29, so I checked ESPN and no forecast was lost.

**Last week's games:** The model picked the right winner in only 2 of 8 games. This is the first full week graded on the new report.
- Right: Arizona beat Iowa State. Oklahoma State beat Colorado.
- Wrong: Kansas beat Baylor 25-24, and the model had given Baylor 63%. It was also wrong on Arizona State over Kansas State, UCF over BYU, Cincinnati over Texas Tech, Utah over Houston, and West Virginia over TCU.
- The miss on the score gap was 6 to 27 points per game.

**Expected wins now (change from last week):**

| Team | Exp wins | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Utah | 10.25 | +0.77 |
| BYU | 9.28 | −1.25 |
| Texas Tech | 9.16 | −1.08 |
| Arizona | 8.94 | +0.75 |
| Houston | 8.94 | −0.84 |
| Oklahoma State | 7.98 | +0.29 |
| Cincinnati | 7.46 | +1.29 |
| UCF | 7.35 | +0.88 |
| West Virginia | 6.37 | +0.80 |
| Kansas State | 6.36 | −0.79 |
| Arizona State | 5.97 | +0.86 |
| **Baylor** | **5.94** | **−0.61** |
| Iowa State | 4.95 | −0.61 |
| Kansas | 4.91 | +1.00 |
| TCU | 4.83 | −0.93 |
| Colorado | 3.31 | −0.53 |

**Baylor:** The forecast is now a 5-7 season (it was 6-6). Tonight's chance to beat UCF went down from 45% to 37%.

**Forecasts that moved:** The biggest swing was Kansas at TCU this Saturday. TCU went up 18 points to a 50% chance. Several other games moved 10 to 17 points.

**Problems:** None. Each team shows "11 games moved", but most of that is small score changes on games already played. The model does this every week.

I updated `docs/STATUS.md`, committed, and pushed (`b353462`). There is nothing for you to do. The next run is Wednesday 2026-11-04: `/forecast-capture`.

"""Evaluate Garrett Horne's 6,002-game file (2019-2025) against actuals and Vegas.

Input:  "2019-2026 All Games.xlsx" (Garrett's email attachment, 2026-07-31).
        Despite the filename it contains 2019-2025 only. One row per game.
        Expected points and win % are the CURRENT model re-run over past games
        (Garrett does not save pregame probabilities), so all accuracy numbers
        are an optimistic upper bound — see EVAL_ALL_GAMES_2019_2025.md.
Joins:  data/cfbd/lines_*.csv on ESPN game id for dates, spreads, totals,
        and moneylines. Home/away orientation is recovered by matching actual
        scores, not the H/@ column (one '(blank)' row exists).

Run:    python evaluate_all_games.py
        Set CFB_BASE to point at a checkout that has the xlsx and data/cfbd
        if running the script from elsewhere.
"""

import glob
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

BASE = os.environ.get('CFB_BASE', os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def load_games():
    df = pd.read_excel(os.path.join(BASE, "2019-2026 All Games.xlsx"))
    df.columns = ['year', 'game_id', 't1', 'ha', 't2', 't1_act', 't2_act',
                  't1_exp', 't2_exp', 't1_wp', 't2_wp']

# Evaluation: Garrett Horne's all-games file, 2019–2025

**Data:** `2019-2026 All Games.xlsx`, emailed by Garrett Horne 2026-07-31 in reply to
our outreach. 6,002 games, 2019–2025 (no 2026 rows despite the filename). One row per
game: actual points, expected points, and % chance of victory for both teams. Clean —
no duplicate game IDs, no nulls, exactly the 87 Baylor games we graded earlier.
Game IDs are ESPN IDs; 6,001 of 6,002 joined to our CFBD lines data (consensus of up
to 5 sportsbooks) for dates, spreads, over/unders, and moneylines.

**The one caveat that governs everything:** Garrett does not save pregame
probabilities. These numbers are the *current* model re-run over past games, with
team ratings that already reflect how those seasons went. Every accuracy number below
is therefore an optimistic upper bound, not an out-of-sample grade. He says he will
start saving pregame probabilities this season — and our Wednesday freeze remains the
only clean pregame record for 2026.

Reproduce with `python evaluate_all_games.py`.

## Finding 1 — The "low-scoring game" bias from the Baylor analysis does not replicate

Our 87-game Baylor analysis found the model running **+8.1 points high in games it
expected to be low-scoring**, concentrated in November. With 6,002 games:

- Total-points bias by expected-total quintile: **+2.6, +2.5, +3.7, +2.7, +2.7** —
  essentially flat. Sliced by *market* over/under instead (which removes the
  regression-to-the-mean artifact of conditioning on the model's own forecast), bias
  actually *rises* with the total: +2.0 (lowest quintile) → +3.6 (highest).
- By month: August +4.5, September +2.5, October +3.1, November +2.8, December +2.5.
  November is not special.

The earlier finding was small-sample noise amplified by slicing on the model's own
prediction. We were right to flag it as unexplained; the explanation is that it isn't
a real structural effect. **Do not repeat the 8.1-point claim to Garrett without this
correction.**

## Finding 2 — The real, robust bias: the model runs ~+2.8 points high on every game

- Overall total-points bias: **+2.82** (p ≈ 1e-51), stable across game types.
- It is shrinking by year: 2019 +3.7, 2020 +4.7, 2021 +3.2, 2022 +2.8, 2023 +2.2,
  2024 +2.4, **2025 +1.6**. A flat correction would over-correct recent seasons;
  the current model's live bias is probably in the +1.5–2.5 range.
- The market over the same games is nearly unbiased (−0.45).
- Smaller secondary effect: the model favors **home teams by about +1 point** of
  margin (+1.23 on true home/away games per the H/@ column, p ≈ 1e-10; +1.05 when
  neutral-site games with an arbitrary CFBD home designation are included) — its
  home-field adjustment is slightly too large.

## Finding 3 — Accuracy is genuinely competitive on points, but hindsight inflates it

- Team points MAE 8.17; margin MAE 11.19; margin r = 0.772; total MAE 11.77.
- Head-to-head on the same 5,971 games: model margin MAE **11.17 vs market 12.17**
  (paired p ≈ 3e-28); total MAE 11.76 vs market 12.64.

Beating the closing spread by a full point per game across six seasons is not a
plausible pregame result — it is the signature of ratings that already know how the
season went. The honest read: the model's *structure* produces market-caliber
predictions, but whether the *pregame* version has edge is exactly what our 2026
frozen captures will answer. (Our July verification of frozen-vs-market on the
published report showed no demonstrated edge: provider MAEs 11.97–12.45.)

"""Grade the 2026 frozen pregame forecasts against results and the betting market.

Input:  data/weekly_forecast_log.csv (every Wednesday capture, append-only)
        data/cfbd/games_2026_regular.csv  (kickoff times, final scores)
        data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv  (open/close spread and total)

dated before the kickoff date; the "earliest" forecast is the first capture
before kickoff. Captures 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14 read a frozen report and
hold 10-02 numbers (docs/STATUS.md), so games graded on them are reported
apart and kept out of the headline.

import os
import re

def norm(name):

def market_sd():
    """SD of (actual home margin - closing line) over 2019-2025, for spread -> win prob."""
    frames = [pd.read_csv(f) for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_20[12][0-9]_regular.csv"))
              if "2026" not in f]
    df = pd.concat(frames)
    resid = (df.homeScore - df.awayScore) + df["lines.0.spread"]
    return float(resid.dropna().std())

    games = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "games_2026_regular.csv"))
    lines = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_2026_regular.csv"))
    n = max(int(c.split(".")[1]) for c in lines.columns if c.startswith("lines.")) + 1
    for col in ["spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]:
        lines[col] = lines[[f"lines.{i}.{col}" for i in range(n)]].mean(axis=1)
    g = games[["id", "week", "startDate", "completed", "homeTeam", "awayTeam",
               "homePoints", "awayPoints"]].merge(
        lines[["id", "spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]], on="id", how="left")
    # Kickoff date in US Central, the clock captured_at is written in.

    g["pair"] = [frozenset((norm(h), norm(a))) for h, a in zip(g.homeTeam, g.awayTeam)]

    r = rows[rows.team.map(norm) == norm(home)]
    flip = r.empty
    r = (rows if flip else r).iloc[0]
    margin, p = r.exp_pts - r.opp_exp_pts, r.win_prob

    by_week = []

        by_week.append({"week": wk, "games": len(w), "model winner": s["winner right"],

"""Grade the 2026 frozen pregame forecasts against results and the betting market.

Input:  data/weekly_forecast_log.csv (every Wednesday capture, append-only)
        data/cfbd/games_2026_regular.csv  (kickoff times, final scores)
        data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv  (open/close spread and total)
        data/cfbd/lines_2019..2025_regular.csv (only to size the spread->prob SD)
Output: EVAL_2026_SEASON.md

One row per game (model game_id). The forecast graded is the latest capture
dated before the kickoff date; the "earliest" forecast is the first capture
before kickoff. Captures 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14 read a frozen report and
hold 10-02 numbers (docs/STATUS.md), so games graded on them are reported
apart and kept out of the headline.

Refresh the CFBD files first: move lines_2026_regular.csv and
games_2026_regular.csv aside, then `python cfbd_pull.py --years 2026 --only lines games`.

Run:    uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python evaluate_2026_season.py
"""

import glob
import os
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CFBD = os.path.join(BASE, "data", "cfbd")
STALE = {"2026-10-07": "2026-10-02", "2026-10-14": "2026-10-02"}


def norm(name):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", str(name).lower().replace("&", "and"))


def market_sd():
    """SD of (actual home margin - closing line) over 2019-2025, for spread -> win prob."""
    frames = [pd.read_csv(f) for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_20[12][0-9]_regular.csv"))
              if "2026" not in f]
    df = pd.concat(frames)
    resid = (df.homeScore - df.awayScore) + df["lines.0.spread"]
    return float(resid.dropna().std())


def load_market():
    games = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "games_2026_regular.csv"))
    # Division II/III teams meet twice in a season; Big 12 games always have an FBS side.
    games = games[(games.homeClassification == "fbs") | (games.awayClassification == "fbs")]
    lines = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_2026_regular.csv"))
    n = max(int(c.split(".")[1]) for c in lines.columns if c.startswith("lines.")) + 1
    for col in ["spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]:
        lines[col] = lines[[f"lines.{i}.{col}" for i in range(n)]].mean(axis=1)
    g = games[["id", "week", "startDate", "completed", "homeTeam", "awayTeam",
               "homePoints", "awayPoints"]].merge(
        lines[["id", "spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]], on="id", how="left")
    # Kickoff date in US Central, the clock captured_at is written in.
    g["kick"] = (pd.to_datetime(g.startDate, utc=True).dt.tz_convert("America/Chicago")
                 .dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
    g["pair"] = [frozenset((norm(h), norm(a))) for h, a in zip(g.homeTeam, g.awayTeam)]
    assert not g.pair.duplicated().any(), "a pair meets twice; join needs a date"
    return g


def orient(rows, home):
    """Model forecast from the home team's side: (p_home, margin, total)."""
    r = rows[rows.team.map(norm) == norm(home)]
    flip = r.empty
    r = (rows if flip else r).iloc[0]
    margin, p = r.exp_pts - r.opp_exp_pts, r.win_prob
    return (1 - p, -margin, r.exp_pts + r.opp_exp_pts) if flip else (p, margin, r.exp_pts + r.opp_exp_pts)


def build():
    log = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(BASE, "data", "weekly_forecast_log.csv"))
    log["asof"] = log.captured_at.map(lambda d: STALE.get(d, d))
    g = load_market().set_index("pair")
    out, unmatched = [], set()
    for gid, rows in log.groupby("game_id"):
        pair = frozenset((norm(rows.team.iloc[0]), norm(rows.opponent.iloc[0])))
        if pair not in g.index:
            unmatched.add(f"{rows.team.iloc[0]} vs {rows.opponent.iloc[0]}")
            continue
        m = g.loc[pair]
        if not m.completed:
            continue
        pre = rows[rows.captured_at < m.kick]
        if pre.empty:
            continue
        last, first = pre.captured_at.max(), pre.captured_at.min()
        p, mg, tot = orient(pre[pre.captured_at == last], m.homeTeam)
        p0, mg0, _ = orient(pre[pre.captured_at == first], m.homeTeam)
        out.append(dict(
            game_id=gid, week=int(m.week), kick=m.kick, home=m.homeTeam, away=m.awayTeam,
            captured=last, asof=STALE.get(last, last), stale=last in STALE,
            lead_days=(pd.Timestamp(m.kick) - pd.Timestamp(STALE.get(last, last))).days,
            p=p, margin=mg, total=tot, p0=p0, margin0=mg0, first=first,
            act_margin=m.homePoints - m.awayPoints, act_total=m.homePoints + m.awayPoints,
            close=-m.spread, open=-m.spreadOpen, ou=m.overUnder, ou_open=m.overUnderOpen))
    df = pd.DataFrame(out)
    df["home_won"] = (df.act_margin > 0).astype(float)
    return df, sorted(unmatched)


def score(df, p, margin, total=None):
    """Pick accuracy, Brier, margin MAE (and total MAE/bias) for one forecast set."""
    pick = np.sign(df[margin]) == np.sign(df.act_margin)
    r = {"games": len(df), "winner right": f"{pick.sum()}/{len(df)} ({pick.mean():.0%})",
         "Brier": ((df[p] - df.home_won) ** 2).mean(),
         "margin MAE": (df[margin] - df.act_margin).abs().mean()}
    if total:
        r["total MAE"] = (df[total] - df.act_total).abs().mean()
        r["total bias"] = (df[total] - df.act_total).mean()
    return r


def table(rows):
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3).to_markdown(index=False)


def main():
    df, unmatched = build()
    sd = market_sd()
    df["p_close"] = stats.norm.cdf(df.close / sd)
    df["p_open"] = stats.norm.cdf(df.open / sd)
    fresh = df[~df.stale]
    lined = fresh.dropna(subset=["close", "open", "ou", "ou_open"])
    stale = df[df.stale]

    md = ["# Evaluation: 2026 frozen pregame forecasts", "",
          f"Regenerate: `uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python evaluate_2026_season.py`.",
          f"Games graded: {len(df)} completed games with a capture before kickoff "
          f"({len(fresh)} on a fresh forecast, {len(stale)} on the stale 10-02 copy). "
          f"Weeks {df.week.min()}-{df.week.max()}. Every number here is a true pregame forecast.", "",
          "Market win probability comes from the spread: P(home) = Phi(line / SD), "
          f"SD = {sd:.1f} points (residual of 2019-2025 closing lines). "
          "The opening line is set before our Wednesday capture; the closing line is set after "
          "it and knows more, so it is the stricter test.", ""]

    md += ["## 1. Model vs the betting market (fresh forecasts, games with a line)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model (Wed capture)", **score(lined, "p", "margin", "total")},
                  {"forecast": "Opening line", **score(lined, "p_open", "open", "ou_open")},
                  {"forecast": "Closing line", **score(lined, "p_close", "close", "ou")}]), ""]
    d_open = (lined.margin - lined.act_margin).abs() - (lined.open - lined.act_margin).abs()
    d_close = (lined.margin - lined.act_margin).abs() - (lined.close - lined.act_margin).abs()
    md += [f"Paired margin-error gap, model minus market (negative = model better): "
           f"vs open {d_open.mean():+.2f} (p = {stats.ttest_1samp(d_open, 0).pvalue:.2f}), "
           f"vs close {d_close.mean():+.2f} (p = {stats.ttest_1samp(d_close, 0).pvalue:.2f}).", ""]

    by_week = []
    for wk, w in lined.groupby("week"):
        s, o = score(w, "p", "margin", "total"), score(w, "p_open", "open")
        by_week.append({"week": wk, "games": len(w), "model winner": s["winner right"],
                        "model margin MAE": s["margin MAE"], "open-line margin MAE": o["margin MAE"],
                        "model Brier": s["Brier"], "open-line Brier": o["Brier"],
                        "model total bias": s["total bias"]})
    md += ["## 2. Week by week (fresh forecasts, games with a line)", "",
           "About 8 games a week: one lucky or unlucky game moves accuracy by 12 points. "
           "Read the trend, not a single week.", "", table(by_week), ""]

    both = fresh[fresh["first"] < fresh.captured]
    md += ["## 3. Did in-season updating help? (same games, earliest vs last pregame forecast)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Earliest capture", **score(both, "p0", "margin0")},
                  {"forecast": "Last capture before kickoff", **score(both, "p", "margin")}]), ""]

    md += ["## 4. Weeks graded on the stale 10-02 copy (not the model's record)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model (10-02 numbers)", **score(stale, "p", "margin", "total")}]), "",
           "## 5. All fresh forecasts, including games with no line (FCS opponents)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model", **score(fresh, "p", "margin", "total")}]), ""]

    md += ["## Unmatched model games (not graded)", ""]
    md += [f"- {u}" for u in unmatched] or ["- none"]
    md += ["", "## Per-game record", "",
           df[["week", "kick", "away", "home", "asof", "lead_days", "p", "margin", "open", "close",
               "act_margin"]].sort_values(["week", "kick"]).round(2).to_markdown(index=False), ""]

    with open(os.path.join(BASE, "EVAL_2026_SEASON.md"), "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(md))
    print("\n".join(md[:60]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

          f"Regenerate: `uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python evaluate_2026_season.py`.",
          f"Games graded: {len(df)} completed games with a capture before kickoff "
          f"({len(fresh)} on a fresh forecast, {len(stale)} on the stale 10-02 copy). "
          f"Weeks {df.week.min()}-{df.week.max()}. Every number here is a true pregame forecast.", "",

          f"SD = {sd:.1f} points (residual of 2019-2025 closing lines). "
          "The opening line is set before our Wednesday capture; the closing line is set after "
          "it and knows more, so it is the stricter test.", ""]

    md += ["## 1. Model vs the betting market (fresh forecasts, games with a line)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model (Wed capture)", **score(lined, "p", "margin", "total")},
                  {"forecast": "Opening line", **score(lined, "p_open", "open", "ou_open")},
                  {"forecast": "Closing line", **score(lined, "p_close", "close", "ou")}]), ""]

    d_close = (lined.margin - lined.act_margin).abs() - (lined.close - lined.act_margin).abs()
    md += [f"Paired margin-error gap, model minus market (negative = model better): "
           f"vs open {d_open.mean():+.2f} (p = {stats.ttest_1samp(d_open, 0).pvalue:.2f}), "
           f"vs close {d_close.mean():+.2f} (p = {stats.ttest_1samp(d_close, 0).pvalue:.2f}).", ""]

    by_week = []
    for wk, w in lined.groupby("week"):
        s, o = score(w, "p", "margin", "total"), score(w, "p_open", "open")
        by_week.append({"week": wk, "games": len(w), "model winner": s["winner right"],
                        "model margin MAE": s["margin MAE"], "open-line margin MAE": o["margin MAE"],
                        "model Brier": s["Brier"], "open-line Brier": o["Brier"],
                        "model total bias": s["total bias"]})
    md += ["## 2. Week by week (fresh forecasts, games with a line)", "",
           "About 8 games a week: one lucky or unlucky game moves accuracy by 12 points. "
           "Read the trend, not a single week.", "", table(by_week), ""]

    both = fresh[fresh["first"] < fresh.captured]
    md += ["## 3. Did in-season updating help? (same games, earliest vs last pregame forecast)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Earliest capture", **score(both, "p0", "margin0")},
                  {"forecast": "Last capture before kickoff", **score(both, "p", "margin")}]), ""]

    md += ["## 4. Weeks graded on the stale 10-02 copy (not the model's record)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model (10-02 numbers)", **score(stale, "p", "margin", "total")}]), "",
           "## 5. All fresh forecasts, including games with no line (FCS opponents)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model", **score(fresh, "p", "margin", "total")}]), ""]

    md += ["## Unmatched model games (not graded)", ""]
    md += [f"- {u}" for u in unmatched] or ["- none"]
    md += ["", "## Per-game record", "",
           df[["week", "kick", "away", "home", "asof", "lead_days", "p", "margin", "open", "close",
               "act_margin"]].sort_values(["week", "kick"]).round(2).to_markdown(index=False), ""]

    with open(os.path.join(BASE, "EVAL_2026_SEASON.md"), "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(md))
    print("\n".join(md[:60]))

"""Grade the 2026 frozen pregame forecasts against results and the betting market.

Input:  data/weekly_forecast_log.csv (every Wednesday capture, append-only)
        data/cfbd/games_2026_regular.csv  (kickoff times, final scores)
        data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv  (open/close spread and total)
        data/cfbd/lines_2019..2025_regular.csv (only to size the spread->prob SD)
Output: EVAL_2026_SEASON.md

One row per game (model game_id). The forecast graded is the latest capture
dated before the kickoff date; the "earliest" forecast is the first capture
before kickoff. Captures 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14 read a frozen report and
hold 10-02 numbers (docs/STATUS.md), so games graded on them are reported
apart and kept out of the headline.

Refresh the CFBD files first: move lines_2026_regular.csv and
games_2026_regular.csv aside, then `python cfbd_pull.py --years 2026 --only lines games`.

Run:    uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python evaluate_2026_season.py
"""

import glob
import os
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CFBD = os.path.join(BASE, "data", "cfbd")
STALE = {"2026-10-07": "2026-10-02", "2026-10-14": "2026-10-02"}


def norm(name):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", str(name).lower().replace("&", "and"))


def market_sd():
    """SD of (actual home margin - closing line) over 2019-2025, for spread -> win prob."""
    frames = [pd.read_csv(f) for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_20[12][0-9]_regular.csv"))
              if "2026" not in f]
    df = pd.concat(frames)
    resid = (df.homeScore - df.awayScore) + df["lines.0.spread"]
    return float(resid.dropna().std())


def load_market():
    games = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "games_2026_regular.csv"))
    # Division II/III teams meet twice in a season; Big 12 games always have an FBS side.
    games = games[(games.homeClassification == "fbs") | (games.awayClassification == "fbs")]
    lines = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_2026_regular.csv"))
    n = max(int(c.split(".")[1]) for c in lines.columns if c.startswith("lines.")) + 1
    for col in ["spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]:
        lines[col] = lines[[f"lines.{i}.{col}" for i in range(n)]].mean(axis=1)
    g = games[["id", "week", "startDate", "completed", "homeTeam", "awayTeam",
               "homePoints", "awayPoints"]].merge(
        lines[["id", "spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]], on="id", how="left")
    # Kickoff date in US Central, the clock captured_at is written in.
    g["kick"] = (pd.to_datetime(g.startDate, utc=True).dt.tz_convert("America/Chicago")
                 .dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
    g["pair"] = [frozenset((norm(h), norm(a))) for h, a in zip(g.homeTeam, g.awayTeam)]
    assert not g.pair.duplicated().any(), "a pair meets twice; join needs a date"
    return g


def orient(rows, home):
    """Model forecast from the home team's side: (p_home, margin, total)."""
    r = rows[rows.team.map(norm) == norm(home)]
    flip = r.empty
    r = (rows if flip else r).iloc[0]
    margin, p = r.exp_pts - r.opp_exp_pts, r.win_prob

"""Grade the 2026 frozen pregame forecasts against results and the betting market.

Input:  data/weekly_forecast_log.csv (every Wednesday capture, append-only)
        data/cfbd/games_2026_regular.csv  (kickoff times, final scores)
        data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv  (open/close spread and total)
        data/cfbd/lines_2019..2025_regular.csv (only to size the spread->prob SD)
Output: EVAL_2026_SEASON.md

One row per game (model game_id). The forecast graded is the latest capture
dated before the kickoff date; the "earliest" forecast is the first capture
before kickoff. Captures 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14 read a frozen report and
hold 10-02 numbers (docs/STATUS.md), so games graded on them are reported
apart and kept out of the headline.

Refresh the CFBD files first: move lines_2026_regular.csv and
games_2026_regular.csv aside, then `python cfbd_pull.py --years 2026 --only lines games`.

Run:    uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python evaluate_2026_season.py
"""

import glob
import os
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CFBD = os.path.join(BASE, "data", "cfbd")
STALE = {"2026-10-07": "2026-10-02", "2026-10-14": "2026-10-02"}


ALIAS = {"samhoustonstate": "samhouston"}  # model name -> CFBD name


def norm(name):
    n = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", str(name).lower().replace("&", "and"))
    return ALIAS.get(n, n)


def market_sd():
    """SD of (actual home margin - closing line) over 2019-2025, for spread -> win prob."""
    frames = [pd.read_csv(f) for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_20[12][0-9]_regular.csv"))
              if "2026" not in f]
    df = pd.concat(frames)
    resid = (df.homeScore - df.awayScore) + df["lines.0.spread"]
    return float(resid.dropna().std())


def load_market():
    games = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "games_2026_regular.csv"))
    # Division II/III teams meet twice in a season; Big 12 games always have an FBS side.
    games = games[(games.homeClassification == "fbs") | (games.awayClassification == "fbs")]
    lines = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CFBD, "lines_2026_regular.csv"))
    n = max(int(c.split(".")[1]) for c in lines.columns if c.startswith("lines.")) + 1
    for col in ["spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]:
        lines[col] = lines[[f"lines.{i}.{col}" for i in range(n)]].mean(axis=1)
    g = games[["id", "week", "startDate", "completed", "conferenceGame", "homeTeam", "awayTeam",
               "homePoints", "awayPoints"]].merge(
        lines[["id", "spread", "spreadOpen", "overUnder", "overUnderOpen"]], on="id", how="left")
    # Kickoff date in US Central, the clock captured_at is written in.
    g["kick"] = (pd.to_datetime(g.startDate, utc=True).dt.tz_convert("America/Chicago")
                 .dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
    g["pair"] = [frozenset((norm(h), norm(a))) for h, a in zip(g.homeTeam, g.awayTeam)]
    assert not g.pair.duplicated().any(), "a pair meets twice; join needs a date"
    return g


def orient(rows, home):
    """Model forecast from the home team's side: (p_home, margin, total)."""
    r = rows[rows.team.map(norm) == norm(home)]
    flip = r.empty
    r = (rows if flip else r).iloc[0]
    margin, p = r.exp_pts - r.opp_exp_pts, r.win_prob
    return (1 - p, -margin, r.exp_pts + r.opp_exp_pts) if flip else (p, margin, r.exp_pts + r.opp_exp_pts)


def build():
    log = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(BASE, "data", "weekly_forecast_log.csv"))
    log["asof"] = log.captured_at.map(lambda d: STALE.get(d, d))
    g = load_market().reset_index(drop=True)
    at = dict(zip(g.pair, g.index))
    out, unmatched = [], set()
    for gid, rows in log.groupby("game_id"):
        pair = frozenset((norm(rows.team.iloc[0]), norm(rows.opponent.iloc[0])))
        if pair not in at:
            unmatched.add(f"{rows.team.iloc[0]} vs {rows.opponent.iloc[0]}")
            continue
        m = g.loc[at[pair]]
        if not m.completed:
            continue
        pre = rows[rows.captured_at < m.kick]
        if pre.empty:
            continue
        last, first = pre.captured_at.max(), pre.captured_at.min()
        p, mg, tot = orient(pre[pre.captured_at == last], m.homeTeam)
        p0, mg0, _ = orient(pre[pre.captured_at == first], m.homeTeam)
        out.append(dict(
            game_id=gid, week=int(m.week), kick=m.kick, home=m.homeTeam, away=m.awayTeam,
            conf=bool(m.conferenceGame),
            captured=last, asof=STALE.get(last, last), stale=last in STALE,
            lead_days=(pd.Timestamp(m.kick) - pd.Timestamp(STALE.get(last, last))).days,
            p=p, margin=mg, total=tot, p0=p0, margin0=mg0, first=first,
            act_margin=m.homePoints - m.awayPoints, act_total=m.homePoints + m.awayPoints,
            close=-m.spread, open=-m.spreadOpen, ou=m.overUnder, ou_open=m.overUnderOpen))
    df = pd.DataFrame(out)
    df["home_won"] = (df.act_margin > 0).astype(float)
    return df, sorted(unmatched)


def score(df, p, margin, total=None):
    """Pick accuracy, Brier, margin MAE (and total MAE/bias) for one forecast set."""
    pick = np.sign(df[margin]) == np.sign(df.act_margin)
    r = {"games": len(df), "winner right": f"{pick.sum()}/{len(df)} ({pick.mean():.0%})",
         "Brier": ((df[p] - df.home_won) ** 2).mean(),
         "margin MAE": (df[margin] - df.act_margin).abs().mean()}
    if total:
        r["total MAE"] = (df[total] - df.act_total).abs().mean()
        r["total bias"] = (df[total] - df.act_total).mean()
    return r


def table(rows):
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3).to_markdown(index=False)


def main():
    df, unmatched = build()
    sd = market_sd()
    df["p_close"] = stats.norm.cdf(df.close / sd)
    df["p_open"] = stats.norm.cdf(df.open / sd)
    fresh = df[~df.stale]
    lined = fresh.dropna(subset=["close", "open", "ou", "ou_open"])
    stale = df[df.stale]

    md = ["# Evaluation: 2026 frozen pregame forecasts", "",
          f"Regenerate: `uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python evaluate_2026_season.py`.",

          f"({len(fresh)} on a fresh forecast, {len(stale)} on the stale 10-02 copy). "

          "Market win probability comes from the spread: P(home) = Phi(line / SD), "
          f"SD = {sd:.1f} points (residual of 2019-2025 closing lines). "
          "The opening line is set before our Wednesday capture; the closing line is set after "
          "it and knows more, so it is the stricter test.", ""]

    md += ["## 1. Model vs the betting market (fresh forecasts, games with a line)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model (Wed capture)", **score(lined, "p", "margin", "total")},
                  {"forecast": "Opening line", **score(lined, "p_open", "open", "ou_open")},
                  {"forecast": "Closing line", **score(lined, "p_close", "close", "ou")}]), ""]
    d_open = (lined.margin - lined.act_margin).abs() - (lined.open - lined.act_margin).abs()
    d_close = (lined.margin - lined.act_margin).abs() - (lined.close - lined.act_margin).abs()
    md += [f"Paired margin-error gap, model minus market (negative = model better): "
           f"vs open {d_open.mean():+.2f} (p = {stats.ttest_1samp(d_open, 0).pvalue:.2f}), "
           f"vs close {d_close.mean():+.2f} (p = {stats.ttest_1samp(d_close, 0).pvalue:.2f}).", ""]

    by_week = []
    for wk, w in lined.groupby("week"):
        s, o = score(w, "p", "margin", "total"), score(w, "p_open", "open")
        by_week.append({"week": wk, "games": len(w), "model winner": s["winner right"],
                        "model margin MAE": s["margin MAE"], "open-line margin MAE": o["margin MAE"],
                        "model Brier": s["Brier"], "open-line Brier": o["Brier"],
                        "model total bias": s["total bias"]})
    md += ["## 2. Week by week (fresh forecasts, games with a line)", "",
           "About 8 games a week: one lucky or unlucky game moves accuracy by 12 points. "
           "Read the trend, not a single week.", "", table(by_week), ""]

    both = fresh[fresh["first"] < fresh.captured]
    md += ["## 3. Did in-season updating help? (same games, earliest vs last pregame forecast)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Earliest capture", **score(both, "p0", "margin0")},
                  {"forecast": "Last capture before kickoff", **score(both, "p", "margin")}]), ""]

    md += ["## 4. Weeks graded on the stale 10-02 copy (not the model's record)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model (10-02 numbers)", **score(stale, "p", "margin", "total")}]), "",
           "## 5. All fresh forecasts, including games with no line (FCS opponents)", "",
           table([{"forecast": "Model", **score(fresh, "p", "margin", "total")}]), ""]

    md += ["## Unmatched model games (not graded)", ""]
    md += [f"- {u}" for u in unmatched] or ["- none"]
    md += ["", "## Per-game record", "",
           df[["week", "kick", "away", "home", "asof", "lead_days", "p", "margin", "open", "close",
               "act_margin"]].sort_values(["week", "kick"]).round(2).to_markdown(index=False), ""]

    with open(os.path.join(BASE, "EVAL_2026_SEASON.md"), "w") as f:

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-10-30 (Fri): Captured 16/16 teams, 12 games each, before Baylor at UCF that night. Wed 10-28 was missed, but no Big 12 game was played Thu 10-29, so nothing was lost. Week 8 graded (first week on the new report): **2 of 8 sides correct**. Right: Arizona over Iowa State, Oklahoma State over Colorado. Wrong: Kansas over Baylor 25-24 (Baylor 63%), Arizona State over Kansas State, UCF over BYU, Cincinnati over Texas Tech, Utah over Houston, West Virginia over TCU. Baylor 5.94 expected wins (raw 5-7), down 0.61; UCF tonight 37% (was 45%). Biggest drops: BYU -1.25, Texas Tech -1.08. Biggest gain: Cincinnati +1.29. Played games also show small projected-score shifts every week, so "moved 11" per team is mostly that noise.
- 2026-10-23 (Fri): **The capture was reading a dead report.** The site moved to a new Power BI report around 10-05 (key `f249bea3-…`); `weekly_capture.py` still opened the old one (`6e6c66a9-…`), which still loads but froze about 10-02. So the 10-07, 10-14 and first 10-23 captures were identical copies of 10-02. `REPORT` now points at the new report (same page `fe8c0d478504c7c16beb`). Eric confirmed the site itself was current.
- 2026-10-23 re-capture with the new report: 16/16 teams, every team moved. Baylor 6.55 expected wins (raw 6-6), Kansas tomorrow 63%. Wed 10-21 was missed, but no Big 12 game was played Thu 10-22 or Fri 10-23, so the week-8 forecast is safe.
- **Lost for good:** the real pre-game forecasts for weeks 6 and 7 (games about 10-10 and 10-17). The 10-07 and 10-14 snapshots hold 10-02 numbers, so the compare grades those games against stale forecasts (week 6: 4/6 sides, week 7: 4/7). Do not count them as the model's record. Week 5 (about 10-03) is graded against the real 10-02 forecast: 4 of 7 sides correct.
- 2026-10-02 (Fri): Captured all 16 Big 12 teams. Week 4 graded: the model picked 6 of 8 unique games right. Misses: Kansas State over Cincinnati (43% Cincinnati; Cincinnati won 31-26) and West Virginia over Oklahoma State (33% Oklahoma State; Oklahoma State won 41-24, 27-pt margin miss). Baylor beat Colorado 23-13 (forecast 30-20, margin miss 0). Baylor is at 6.73 expected wins (raw 6-6), up 0.37. Model re-rated Oklahoma State and UCF up, Kansas State and West Virginia down.
- The 9/30 Wednesday capture was skipped. No forecast was lost: no games were played between 9/26 and 10/2 (no Week 5 game shows as played).
- `scripts/weekly_run.sh` now skips the comparison when the capture fails (3619c54). Before, a failed capture printed last week's comparison as if it were new.
- Playwright auto-updated and now needs browser build `chromium-1243`. It is installed on the Mac. See `docs/handoffs/2026-09-23-week3-capture.md`.
- Snapshots are in `data/weekly_snapshots/`, and copies plus comparison reports are in `../CFB_Forecast_Archive/2026/`.

## Next
1. Run the next Big 12 capture on Wednesday 2026-11-04: `scripts/weekly_run.sh` (or `/forecast-capture`). Run it headed, from the main checkout, on the Mac. Check ESPN first for Thursday/Friday Big 12 games that week.
2. On 11-04, check the compare: during the season every team should move. If none move, check `REPORT` against the iframe on https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/ before blaming the site.

## Open questions
- ~~`worktree-eval-all-games`: merge or delete?~~ Deleted 2026-09-23. All five of its files were already on `main`, byte-identical. Tip was b863846.
- ~~What made Windows capture Baylor at 07:37 on 9/23?~~ Answered 2026-09-23: no capture task exists on Windows. The daily `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` popup (07:25) prompted a manual run. That task is now disabled on Windows.

## Gotchas
- `uv run --with playwright` pulls the newest playwright. When it updates, the capture dies with `Executable doesn't exist at .../chromium-<N>`. Fix: `uv run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium`, then re-run.
- **The Mac owns the weekly capture (decided 2026-09-23).** Never run it on Windows. Two machines writing the same day's snapshot and `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` conflict at the next sync.
- Run the capture from the main checkout, not a worktree. `ARCHIVE = ROOT.parent / "CFB_Forecast_Archive"` resolves to the wrong folder inside `.claude/worktrees/`, so use `--no-archive` there and copy by hand.
- A capture must run headed. A dropdown's search box renders about 1s after the click, and the script waits for it. If it fails with `search box never appeared`, the report UI changed.
- One failed attempt per team is normal; the retry recovers it.
- **"No forecast moved" in season means a dead report link, not a stale site.** The site can swap its Power BI report; the old link keeps loading frozen data with no error. Get the live link: `curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/ | grep -o 'app.powerbi.com/view?r=[^"&]*'` and compare with `REPORT` in `weekly_capture.py`. Found 2026-10-23 after three frozen captures.

- 2026-09-10: Captured and froze Baylor's forecast (4.49 expected wins). Auburn graded as a correct side with a 3-point margin miss.

content.text:
**The model has not improved this season.** Compared with the betting line, it was a little worse almost every week, and the gap did not shrink.

I graded 68 games, using the forecast we froze before each kickoff. I compared each one to the final score and to the betting line.

**Model vs. the opening betting line (67 games that had a line):**

| | Model | Opening line |
|---|---|---|
| Picked the winner | 51/67 (76%) | 54/67 (81%) |
| Average miss on the score gap | 12.9 pts | 11.4 pts |
| Probability score (Brier: lower is better) | 0.157 | 0.125 |

- **Week by week:** The model did worse than the line in 5 of 6 weeks, by 1 to 4.5 points a game. There is no trend toward getting better.
- **Why it looks much worse in October:** The win-pick rate fell from 87% in week 1 to 25% in week 8. Most of that drop is because conference games are harder to call than early games against weak teams. The line's rate fell too. In conference games the model picked 11 of 22 winners, and the line picked 14 of 22.
- **Do the weekly updates help?** A little, but the result is mixed. From week 4 on, the score-gap miss went from 16.0 points (pre-season forecast) to 14.3 points (last forecast). But it picked fewer winners: 12 of 23, down from 14.
- **Old bias still there:** The model guesses total points about 2.1 too high. The 2019–2025 review found 2.8. In conference games it is 6.2 too high, but 22 games is too few to be sure. The betting line is close to 0.

**How sure we can be:**
- 67 games is a small sample. The model's gap behind the line is not yet a sure result (p = 0.09).
- Only 23 games were played after week 3.
- Weeks 6 and 7 are left out: their 13 games were graded against the old 10-02 forecast copy. On those, the model picked 8 of 13.

**Files** (in `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/`):
- Full report with a row for every game: `EVAL_2026_SEASON.md`
- Script: `evaluate_2026_season.py`
- To run it again: `uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python evaluate_2026_season.py`. First refresh the 2026 games and lines from CFBD (collegefootballdata.com); the steps are at the top of the script.
- Pushed to GitHub (commit `5359d65`). The findings are also in `docs/STATUS.md`.

**What I did not check:**
- I did not check calibration (whether the model's percentages come true as often as they say). There are too few games.
- I got the betting line's win chance from the point spread, not from the betting odds.
- My check that our log and CFBD agree compared the size of each win (81 of 81 match), not which team won. Spot checks of single games show the sides are right.

result: Across 68 graded 2026 games, the model has not improved. It trails the opening betting line (76% vs 81% winners picked; 12.9 vs 11.4 points average score miss) by about the same amount every week, and still guesses total points about 2 too high. The report is in `EVAL_2026_SEASON.md`.

# CFB Victory Model

Weekly forecast capture and evaluation for the college football Victory Model,
Baylor 2026 season.

## The one thing that matters

**The weekly forecast must be frozen every Wednesday, and it cannot be backfilled.**
The published Power BI report is overwritten each week and keeps no history, so a
missed Wednesday is gone permanently. That constraint is the reason this project
exists in the form it does.

Capture window: **2026-08-26 through 2027-01-20** — 22 capture Wednesdays. The start
is the Wednesday *before* the first Saturday games, so Week 1 is frozen before anyone
kicks off.

Run it with the `/forecast-capture` skill, or directly:

```
python weekly_capture.py
```

It takes no arguments. Baylor, 2026, and the output paths are fixed.

## Setup

```
cp .env.example .env      # then add your CFBD API key
python cfbd_pull.py       # idempotent; skips files already present
```

Every CFBD endpoint returns 401 without a key.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `weekly_capture.py` | Loads the published report as a browser, sets slicers, reads the rendered table, writes a dated snapshot plus an append-only log |
| `cfbd_pull.py` | CFBD API puller — 10 datasets, 2019–2026 |
| `compare_snapshots.py` | Diffs week over week |
----
# The Victory Model — What It Is, What It Isn't, and How To Use It

**Audience:** Head coach, coordinators, support staff
**Runtime:** 3 minutes spoken, or one slide
**Prepared:** 2026-07-26

---

## The 30-second version

> "The model can't tell you who wins. It can tell you which games are actually
> in play — and this year, half our schedule is. That's the whole point of
> showing it to you. It's not a crystal ball. It's a triage tool. It tells us
> where our week-to-week effort actually moves the needle."

---

## The 3-minute spoken version

**Lead with the answer.**

"Our season comes down to six games. Not twelve. Six. I'm going to show you
which ones and how we know.

**First, what this thing actually does.**
2026-09-10-baylor-forecast-capture.md
2026-09-16-big12-capture-fix.md
2026-09-23-week3-capture.md
2026-10-02-week4-capture.md
2026-10-23-week8-capture.md

input.args:
--background Audit a third-party college football forecast model and find corrections that measurably improve it. Repo: /Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model (work in place).

CONTEXT
- The model is Garrett Horne's cfbvictorymodel.com. We cannot see or retrain its internals. We only have its outputs per game: expected points for each team (exp_pts, opp_exp_pts) and win probability (win_prob), plus opp_plus_minus (opponent rating) and opp_model_rank. "Improve" therefore means (a) a post-hoc adjustment layer on its outputs that we can apply ourselves, and (b) concrete, evidence-backed diagnoses we can send to Garrett.
- Use for Baylor: a coach triage tool ("which games are actually in play"), so honest win probabilities and margins matter more than totals.
- Read first: EVAL_ALL_GAMES_2019_2025.md + evaluate_all_games.py (6,002 games, 2019-2025, joined to betting lines), EVAL_2026_SEASON.md + evaluate_2026_season.py (2026 true pregame forecasts), docs/STATUS.md.
- Data: "2019-2026 All Games.xlsx" (2019-2025; these are the CURRENT model re-run over past seasons, so hindsight-inflated; good for structural biases, optimistic for accuracy). data/weekly_forecast_log.csv (every 2026 weekly capture; the true pregame record; captures 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14 are stale copies of 2026-10-02, exclude them as evaluate_2026_season.py does). data/cfbd/ (games, lines with open/close spread and totals, 2019-2026; advanced stats, talent, returning production, SP+).
- Known so far: model trails the 2026 opening line (margin MAE 12.9 vs 11.4 over 67 games; Brier 0.157 vs 0.125); total-points bias about +2.1 in 2026 (+2.8 over 2019-25, shrinking by year); home-field about +1 pt too large (2019-25); FCS opponents use a hardcoded -34.13 placeholder rating.

TASK
1. Diagnose where the errors come from. At least check: total bias; home-field / neutral-site handling; whether win_prob is calibrated and consistent with the expected margin (is the implied margin SD right?); over- or under-confidence (should margins shrink toward 0 or toward the market?); early-season vs late-season (preseason priors); conference vs non-conference; FCS placeholder; large-favorite vs close games.
2. Propose and TEST simple corrections (bias shift, home-field shift, margin shrink factor, probability recalibration such as logistic/Platt on the margin, a blend with the opening line). Keep each correction to a few parameters.
3. Validation must be honest: fit on 2019-2024, test on 2025 (hindsight data), then test on the 2026 pregame games, which are the only out-of-sample truth. Report effect on margin MAE, total MAE, Brier, and winner picks on each test set, with uncertainty (bootstrap or paired test). Say plainly when 2026 (~68 games) is too small to confirm a gain. Do not tune anything on the 2026 games.
4. For the market blend, note it is only useful if the opening line is available at forecast time (Wednesday); that is our use case.

DELIVERABLES (do not change existing scripts or data files; do not git commit)
- audit_model.py: reproducible, run with `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with numpy --with openpyxl --with tabulate python audit_model.py`. Read-only on data/.
- docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md: open with the 3-5 corrections ranked by verified out-of-sample gain, each with its numbers on 2025 and 2026; then diagnoses; then a short "what to send Garrett" list; then what did not work. Plain language, short.
Environment: macOS, Python is PEP 668 managed, use uv as above, no global pip. No network needed.

# Model audit — 2026-10-30

## Corrections, ranked by 2026 evidence

**Use the opening line as a second forecast for coach triage.** It gave the best 2026 win chances in this test. Keep collecting frozen forecasts before making a permanent change. The 67-game test is small. We tested several fixes, so a good result may occur by chance. None has a confirmed gain in both a clean 2025 test and a clean 2026 test: the 2025 data has hindsight.

The table gives margin error, total error, Brier score, and correct winner picks, in that order. Lower error and Brier are better. Brier measures the error in win chances; 0 is best. Each row uses the same games in its year. Error means average absolute error, in points.

| Rank and forecast | 2025: 933 games, with hindsight | 2026: 67 true pregame games |
|---|---|---|
| Original model | 10.589 / 11.255 / 0.126 / 788 | 12.940 / 14.134 / 0.157 / 51 |
| 1. Opening line and opening total | 11.962 / 12.532 / 0.157 / 721 | 11.366 / 13.396 / 0.125 / 54 |
| 2. Small opening-line blend | 10.556 / 11.255 / 0.112 / 790 | 12.772 / 14.134 / 0.157 / 51 |
| 3. Lower total by 3.04 | 10.589 / 11.180 / 0.126 / 788 | 12.940 / 14.031 / 0.157 / 51 |
| 4. Refit win chances from margin | 10.589 / 11.255 / 0.110 / 788 | 12.940 / 14.134 / 0.162 / 51 |

- **Opening line:** Its 2026 Brier gain was 0.032. A paired 95% interval for the change was -0.055 to -0.009. Its margin error fell 1.575 points, with an interval of -3.362 to +0.157. The market win chance is an estimate from the spread, not a quoted moneyline. The market lost to the hindsight model in 2025. The test does not prove it will win in future seasons.
- **Blend:** Use 92.83% model margin and 7.17% opening margin. Convert that margin to a win chance with `1 / (1 + exp(-0.16240 * margin))`. The 2026 margin error fell 0.169 points. Its paired 95% interval was -0.306 to -0.038. In 2025 it fell 0.033, with an interval of -0.069 to +0.006. The blend changes both margin and win chance; its Brier gain in 2025 mainly reflects the probability refit. The 2026 Brier change was near zero, with an interval of -0.019 to +0.022. This is a small gain after several tests, not proof of future benefit.
- **Total shift:** Subtract 3.04 from the game total, or 1.52 from each team. The 2026 total error fell 0.103 points, with an interval of -0.798 to +0.592. The 2025 change was -0.075, with an interval of -0.265 to +0.108. Neither confirms a gain. The historical bias is shrinking, so this shift may be too large today.
- **Win chance refit:** Use `1 / (1 + exp(-0.16987 * margin))`. The 2025 Brier gain was 0.016, with an interval of -0.020 to -0.012. The 2026 Brier change was +0.005, with an interval of -0.016 to +0.028. The apparent 2025 gain is likely helped by hindsight. Do not adopt this refit yet.

For the opening-line forecast, `P(home win) = normal CDF(opening home margin / 15.53933)`. The margin is positive when the home team is favored. For the blend and refit, use the same home-margin sign. These formulas are symmetric: swap the teams and the win chance becomes `1 - P`. A blend or market forecast is useful only when that opening line was available by the Wednesday forecast. The files do not record line publication times, so we could not verify availability for each game. Do not substitute a closing line.

All fitted values came from 2019–2024 only. The opening line is a fixed comparison, not a weight chosen from 2026. The 2025 data is a current model rerun with knowledge of the season. The 2026 data is the only true pregame test. It covers Big 12 captures, not all college games. The script excludes the stale 10-07 and 10-14 captures as the prior evaluation does. Each interval comes from 5,000 paired game resamples. The intervals do not account for testing several fixes. The full script output includes intervals for all four measures and all candidates.

## Diagnoses

- **Totals:** The 2019–2024 bias was +3.04 points. It fell to +1.60 in 2025. In all 68 fresh 2026 games it was +1.76; in the 67 games with an opening total it was +2.13. This is a real historical pattern, but its present size is uncertain.
- **Home and neutral sites:** In 2019–2024, true home teams had a +1.44 margin bias across 4,710 games. Neutral games had -0.32 across 358. In 2025 the home bias was only +0.15. In 2026 it was -6.28 across 64; there were only four neutral games. The old home effect does not justify a fixed live correction. FCS games affect the home average.
- **Win chance versus margin:** The median implied normal spread of game margins was 18.75 points in training and 20.21 in 2026. The actual margin error spread was 14.38 and 16.55, respectively. This comparison assumes normal errors and constant spread; it does not prove the published win formula uses that distribution. In 2025 favorites rated 60–70% won 87.2% of 203 games, a hindsight result. In 2026 they won 60.9% of 23 games. Those 23 games cannot establish calibration.
- **Early and late:** In 2026, model versus opening-line margin error was 12.58 versus 11.46 in weeks 1–3, and 14.35 versus 11.79 in week 4 onward. The later group has only 23 games. For the same later games, earliest versus last pregame model error was 16.00 versus 14.35. This does not identify a faulty preseason prior: we cannot see the model inputs, and both time and game mix change.
- **Conference:** In 2026, conference games had +6.23 total bias across 22 games. Non-conference games had -0.37 across 46. The difference is too small a sample to set a separate correction. The model trailed the opening line on margin error in both groups: 12.50 versus 11.05 and 13.50 versus 11.83.
- **FCS:** The log contains 45 forecast rows with the exact -34.13 opponent rating; these are repeated captures, not 45 games. In 16 fresh 2026 FCS games, margin error was 15.25 versus 11.78 for the opening line. The placeholder is a plausible source of error, not proof of cause. FCS teams differ in strength.
- **Close and large favorites:** In 2026, games with model margins of 0–7 points had 12.35 margin error across 20 games and Brier 0.255. Games above 21 points had 16.00 margin error across 21 games and Brier 0.047. Large favorites can have easy winner picks and poor score margins at the same time. Do not treat these small groups as stable estimates.

## What to send Garrett

1. The total forecast ran +3.04 points high in 2019–2024, then +1.60 in 2025. Please check the scoring baseline and whether it changes by season.
2. The old home-margin bias was +1.44 points, but it was +0.15 in 2025. Please check true home versus neutral handling and FCS effects before changing home field.
3. Please check the fixed -34.13 FCS rating against individual FCS teams. Our 16 fresh 2026 FCS games had 15.25-point margin error versus 11.78 for the opening line.
4. Please save every forecast before kickoff, including win chance, expected scores, team ratings, venue and timestamp. Hindsight reruns cannot establish pregame calibration or an edge.

## What did not work

- Subtracting the fitted 1.44 points from the home margin made 2026 margin error worse: 12.940 to 13.462. The paired change interval was +0.207 to +0.823. It also reduced picks from 51 to 49. It did not alter win chances in this isolated test, so it is not a complete forecast recipe.
- Shrinking every margin toward zero by multiplying by 0.94512 changed 2026 error from 12.940 to 13.197. The paired change interval was -0.051 to +0.559. It did not alter win chances in this isolated test. Do not apply it.
- The probability refit improved the hindsight test but not the clean 2026 test. Do not make probabilities more extreme based on hindsight.

## Run again

```sh
/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with numpy --with openpyxl --with tabulate python audit_model.py
```

The script reads the existing spreadsheet and files in `data/`. It does not write to them. It prints all results; it does not update this report.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
d=pd.read_csv("data/weekly_forecast_log.csv")
d=d[d.captured_at=="2026-10-23"].copy()
# team's own rating = opp_plus_minus seen in opponents' rows (same capture)
own=d.groupby("opponent").opp_plus_minus.first()
d["own"]=d.team.map(own)
d=d[d.actual_pts.isna()].dropna(subset=["own"])   # unplayed only: pregame numbers
d["m"]=d.exp_pts-d.opp_exp_pts; d["diff"]=d.own-d.opp_plus_minus
v=d.venue.map({"H":1,"A":-1,"N":0})
X=np.c_[d["diff"],v]; b,res,*_=np.linalg.lstsq(X,d.m,rcond=None)
pred=X@b
print("rows",len(d),"coef diff,venue",b.round(3),"R2",round(1-((d.m-pred)**2).sum()/((d.m-d.m.mean())**2).sum(),4),"max abs resid",round(abs(d.m-pred).max(),2))
# win prob vs margin
from math import erf,sqrt
for sd in [14,16,18,20]:
    p=0.5*(1+np.vectorize(erf)(d.m/(sd*sqrt(2)))); print("sd",sd,"wp MAE",round(abs(p-d.win_prob).mean(),3))
print(d[["team","opponent","venue","own","opp_plus_minus","exp_pts","opp_exp_pts","win_prob"]].head(6).to_string())
PY

**No, we can't use REA on this model.** REA takes apart program files, and we don't have Garrett's program. We only see the Power BI report it posts.

**But we have enough to work out how the model is built.** I tested it on 47 games from the 10-23 capture:
- **Predicted score gap ≈ 0.77 × (team rating − opponent rating) + 2.5 points for the home team.** This explains 94% of its forecasts.
- **Win chance = a bell curve with a spread of about 20 points.** It matches the posted win chances to within about 1 point of percentage.

So the model is three parts: team ratings, a home-field edge, and a win-chance curve.

**Why rebuilding it won't help much:**
- Codex already tested changes to the home edge and the win-chance curve. Neither helped this season.
- The weak part is the **team ratings**. That is where the betting line beats the model.
- We can't fix his ratings, because we can't see what goes into them.

**Ways to improve it, best first:**
1. **Use the opening betting line next to the model** for the coach view. It is the only gain we have proof of. It costs nothing.
2. **Ask Garrett for help.** He owns the ratings and has shared data before. Send him the 4 fixes from the audit, plus our rebuild of his math. Ask how his ratings are made and what weight he gives the pre-season ratings.
3. **Build our own team ratings from the CFBD data** (team strength, talent, returning players). This is a big project. It would probably still not beat the betting line, and it is mid-season. I would not start it now.

**Pick one:**
- **A. Do 1 and 2 (my pick):** add the opening-line win chance to the coach view, and send the note to Garrett.
- **B. Do only 2:** send the note, then wait for his answer before you change anything.

Not checked: I tested only one week of data. The rule does not fit every game exactly. Some games are off by up to 5 points, so the model may have a part we can't see.

The finding is in `docs/STATUS.md` (commit `c2c7ab2`).

Use the `gws` CLI (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gws`) as the default way to interact with Google services. Do not export its credentials or call Google APIs directly with tokens.

**Why:** Eric said so on 2026-10-22 ("use gws-cli as the default way to interact with google") after I tried to speed up Drive wave 2 by exporting the gws OAuth login and calling the Drive API over HTTPS; the auto-mode classifier also denied that.

**How to apply:** Script Google work as `gws <service> <resource> <method>` subprocess calls, parsing stdout only (stderr carries a keyring line). Each call takes about 2.5 s, and more threads do not help (4 and 12 threads both gave ~70 files/min on 10-22), so plan long jobs as overnight runs. Traps (2026-10-29): a download (`files get` with `"alt":"media"` and `-o <file>`) must land inside gws's working directory, or it fails with "outside the current directory": run gws with `cwd=` the target folder and a bare file name. Uploading new content to an existing file is `files update --upload <path> --upload-content-type <mime>`; compare the returned `md5Checksum` with the local `md5 -q`. Content search is `"q": "fullText contains '...'"` (~2 s, PDFs included); `drive_index.py find --inside` wraps it. Related: [[drive-fuse-read-hang]], [[gws-forms-api]].

# Draft reply to Garrett Horne

**To:** cfbvictorymodel@gmail.com
**Status:** Draft — review before sending.
**Context:** His 2026-07-31 reply attached "2019-2026 All Games.xlsx" (6,002 games,
2019–2025, current-model expected points and win %). Full analysis in
`EVAL_ALL_GAMES_2019_2025.md`.

---

**Subject:** Re: Independent validation of your model — results from all 6,002 games

Garrett,

Thank you — this is exactly what I needed, and I've now run the full file. Three
things worth your time, including one correction to my own earlier claim.

**First, the correction.** In my original email I told you the model ran 8.1 points
high in games it expected to be low-scoring, concentrated in November. With all 6,002
games instead of Baylor's 87, that finding does not replicate. The bias is flat
across expected totals (+2.5 to +3.7 in every quintile) and flat across months.
My Baylor sample was too small, and slicing on the model's own prediction amplified
the noise. Consider that thread closed.

**What is real is simpler: a uniform over-prediction of scoring.** Across all games
the model runs +2.8 points high on the game total (p ≈ 1e-51 — not noise). The good
news is it's shrinking every year: +3.7 in 2019 down to +1.6 in 2025, so whatever
you've been adjusting is working. A ~1-point-per-team trim on expected points would
zero out what's left. Separately, home teams are favored by about a point more than
results justify (+1.2 on true home/away games), so your home-field adjustment could
come down slightly.

**On accuracy, a caveat you'll appreciate.** Against the closing consensus line over
the same games, the file's predictions win: margin MAE 11.17 vs 12.17, and the win
percentages beat the devigged moneyline on Brier score. But since these come from the
current model re-run over past seasons — as you said, the pregame probabilities
weren't saved — the ratings partly already know how those seasons went, so I'd treat
those wins as an upper bound rather than proof of edge. The same signature shows in
calibration: games your model calls 60–70% go to the favorite 81% of the time. If the
saved pregame numbers land closer to the stated probabilities next year, that gap was
hindsight; if not, your probabilities are genuinely too timid and could be sharpened.

That's why I'm glad you're going to start saving the pregame probabilities this
season — that's the single change that makes the model gradable for real. For what
it's worth I'm freezing your published Baylor forecast every Wednesday this fall, so
between us there will finally be a true out-of-sample record. Happy to share my
capture file at season's end, and to run this same analysis on your saved 2026
numbers next January.

Thanks again for sharing the data — few model authors would.

Eric
----

=== 19fac302c4508f5d
Good evening, Eric,

First of all, thank you for reaching out. It's very rewarding to hear that
someone within the college athletics community is utilizing the model!

I'd be happy to provide all of the predictions from the model. There are
6,002 games spanning 2019–2025.

Unfortunately, I don't currently save the pregame probabilities. You aren't
the first person to bring that up, so I'm likely going to start doing that
this upcoming season (even if it's just stored offline). I did, however,
attach the current model expected win percentages for all games from
2019–2025.

As for the team ratings, they are updated weekly based on current-season
results. Preseason rankings are based on updated roster information and
recent season results. During the month of September, I phase out the
preseason rankings each week. By October, the predictions are based
entirely on the current season.

By all means, please share any feedback or notes you are willing to share!

Thanks,
Garrett Horne
cfbvictorymodel.com

=== 19fa9661dab0993b
Hi,

We've been following your site for a few years now, and it's become one of
the tools we look at frequently.

What we did: pulled every one of our games off the Team Schedule Overview
page, 2019 through 2025, 87 games, and compared predicted scores to results.
Looks like predicted score typically lands within about 7 points, margin
within about 10, and predicted margin correlates with actual margin at r =
0.80. Against a naive baseline, it cuts margin error by roughly 37%. I
thought you might be interested to know that.

We're interested in investigating your model further, which leads to the
ask, and please feel free to decline:

   1. Would you be open to sharing game-level data, predictions, and
   results across all teams rather than just Baylor? With 87 games, I can
   only reliably detect errors larger than about 5 points, and this one is
   around 8. All teams would be roughly 10,000 games, enough to actually track
   it down rather than speculate.
   2. Do you keep the pre-game win probabilities anywhere? On
completed seasons,
   the Chance of Victory column appears to show the realized outcome rather
   than the original forecast, so I haven't been able to evaluate them. I'd
   love to, since probabilities are arguably the most interesting output a
   model like this produces.

I'm glad to send back everything I generate in whatever form is useful, and
I have a few small notes on the report columns you may already know about.
If the answer is no on either count, I completely understand. I've gotten a
lot out of the site regardless and will continue to follow it.

One question if you have a moment: are the team ratings fit on full-season
results, or recomputed week by week?

Thanks for building this and keeping it free.

Eric Rash
eric.rash11@gmail.com

#!/bin/bash
# Weekly CFB Victory Model freeze - all 16 Big 12 teams, then the comparison.
#
# Run it Wednesday of a game week. A Chrome window opens; that is required, not
# a bug. Headless breaks the Power BI team slicer.
#
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh                       # all Big 12, 2026
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU    # just these two
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --year 2027
#
# Snapshots land in data/weekly_snapshots/ and are copied to
# ../CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/ along with each team's comparison text.
set -euo pipefail

# Background/launchd shells get a minimal PATH, so nothing here relies on it.
UV=/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Without this, Python block-buffers stdout whenever the run is redirected to a
# file, so a 10-minute run shows nothing until it finishes.
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Capture exits non-zero if any team failed both passes. Skip the comparison
# then: it diffs whatever snapshots are newest, so after a failed capture it
# prints last week's numbers as if they were today's. Captures are idempotent,
# so fix the cause and re-run (or --teams <the failed ones>).
echo "=== capture ==="
rc=0
"$UV" run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py "$@" || rc=$?

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo
    echo "=== comparison SKIPPED: capture failed (exit $rc) ==="
    echo "Fix the error above and re-run. Nothing was compared or archived."
    exit "$rc"
fi

echo
echo "=== comparison ==="
"$UV" run python compare_snapshots.py --all --archive

exit $rc

"""Model vs opening line for the coming week's games, from the newest capture.

The 2026 audit (docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md) found the opening line was the
better 2026 forecast, so coaches see both side by side. Big gaps are the games
where the two disagree and are worth a second look.

Needs a fresh data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv (scripts/weekly_run.sh pulls it).
shortcut: reads 2026 CFBD files only (via evaluate_2026_season); make the season a
parameter when the 2027 capture starts.

Run:    uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python market_view.py
"""

import os

import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import evaluate_2026_season as ev

BIG_GAP = 0.15  # flag games where the two win chances differ by 15+ points


def main():
    log = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(ev.BASE, "data", "weekly_forecast_log.csv"))
    cap = log.captured_at.max()
    rows = log[(log.captured_at == cap) & log.actual_pts.isna()]
    g = ev.load_market().reset_index(drop=True)
    at = dict(zip(g.pair, g.index))
    sd = ev.market_sd()
    week_end = (pd.Timestamp(cap) + pd.Timedelta(days=7)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

    out = []
    for gid, r in rows.groupby("game_id"):
        pair = frozenset((ev.norm(r.team.iloc[0]), ev.norm(r.opponent.iloc[0])))
        if pair not in at:
            continue
        m = g.loc[at[pair]]
        if not cap <= m.kick <= week_end:
            continue
        p, margin, _ = ev.orient(r, m.homeTeam)
        line = None if pd.isna(m.spreadOpen) else stats.norm.cdf(-m.spreadOpen / sd)
        out.append({"kickoff": m.kick, "game": f"{m.awayTeam} at {m.homeTeam}",
                    "model home win": f"{p:.0%}",
                    "line home win": "no line yet" if line is None else f"{line:.0%}",
                    "model margin": f"{margin:+.0f}",
                    "open line": "" if line is None else f"{-m.spreadOpen:+.1f}",
                    "gap": None if line is None else p - line})

    print(f"MODEL vs OPENING LINE - capture {cap}, games through {week_end}")
    if not out:
        print("  no captured games this week")
        return
    df = pd.DataFrame(out)
    df["flag"] = ["CHECK" if gp is not None and abs(gp) >= BIG_GAP else "" for gp in df.gap]
    df["gap"] = [("" if gp is None else f"{gp:+.0%}") for gp in df.gap]
    print(df.sort_values("kickoff").to_markdown(index=False))
    print(f"Margins are home minus away. Line win chance = Normal(open line / {sd:.1f}). "
          f"CHECK = the two disagree by {BIG_GAP:.0%}+; the line was the better 2026 forecast.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Model vs opening line for the coming week's games, from the newest capture.

The 2026 audit (docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md) found the opening line was the
better 2026 forecast, so coaches see both side by side. Big gaps are the games
where the two disagree and are worth a second look.

Needs a fresh data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv (scripts/weekly_run.sh pulls it).
shortcut: reads 2026 CFBD files only (via evaluate_2026_season); make the season a
parameter when the 2027 capture starts.

Run:    uv run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python market_view.py
"""

import os

import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import evaluate_2026_season as ev

BIG_GAP = 0.15  # flag games where the two win chances differ by 15+ points


def main():
    log = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(ev.BASE, "data", "weekly_forecast_log.csv"))
    cap = log.captured_at.max()
    rows = log[(log.captured_at == cap) & log.actual_pts.isna()]
    g = ev.load_market().reset_index(drop=True)
    at = dict(zip(g.pair, g.index))
    sd = ev.market_sd()
    week_end = (pd.Timestamp(cap) + pd.Timedelta(days=7)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

    out = []
    for gid, r in rows.groupby("game_id"):
        pair = frozenset((ev.norm(r.team.iloc[0]), ev.norm(r.opponent.iloc[0])))
        if pair not in at:
            continue
        m = g.loc[at[pair]]
        if not cap <= m.kick <= week_end:
            continue
        p, margin, _ = ev.orient(r, m.homeTeam)
        line = None if pd.isna(m.spreadOpen) else stats.norm.cdf(-m.spreadOpen / sd)
        out.append({"kickoff": m.kick, "game": f"{m.awayTeam} at {m.homeTeam}",
                    "model home win": f"{p:.0%}",
                    "line home win": "no line yet" if line is None else f"{line:.0%}",
                    "model margin": f"{margin:+.0f}",
                    "open line": "" if line is None else f"{-m.spreadOpen:+.1f}",
                    "gap": None if line is None else p - line})

    print(f"MODEL vs OPENING LINE - capture {cap}, games through {week_end}")
    if not out:
        print("  no captured games this week")
        return
    df = pd.DataFrame(out)
    df["flag"] = ["CHECK" if gp is not None and abs(gp) >= BIG_GAP else "" for gp in df.gap]
    df["gap"] = [("" if gp is None else f"{gp:+.0%}") for gp in df.gap]
    print(df.sort_values("kickoff").to_markdown(index=False))
    print(f"Margins are home minus away. Line win chance = Normal(open line / {sd:.1f}). "
          f"CHECK = the two disagree by {BIG_GAP:.0%}+; the line was the better 2026 forecast.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command for the end-of-day sequence: loose ends → memory → STATUS and handoff → commit and push → one verdict.

Run every step without pausing: invoking closeout authorizes the whole sequence. Commit and push is
standing-authorized for every DEV repo (each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine ends with it, and
unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other). On Windows or in Cowork,
read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Scope.** Every DEV repo with uncommitted or unpushed work (touched this session or not), plus
`~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory`.
A repo whose `CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local (DexaProject is the precedent) is committed,
not pushed, and listed.

**Clear to sign off when** the closing `where-was-i.py --sweep` (step 4) shows no `ACTION` line
except repos listed under "Still open" with their reason, no background job is still writing,
`.errors.log` is empty or its entries are reported, and every repo touched today has a STATUS entry
dated today with a concrete first `## Next` item, and every `card-check` gap is fixed. Questions
only Eric can answer (a receiver nobody named, a decision recorded under `## Open questions`) do
not block: `/startup` shows them tomorrow; list them under "Still open" and say "Clear to sign off".
Anything short of that: "Not clear", naming the one thing blocking.

If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and
note it. A risky fix goes under "Still open".

## Step 1 — Sweep

---
name: cfb-forecast-capture
description: "CFB Victory Model weekly forecast freeze — all 16 Big 12 teams via scripts/weekly_run.sh, archive mirror, Monday-anchored check 2026-08-24 to 2027-01-23 (logged only, no nag since 2026-09-24), Mac only, no backfill, and how to tell a real missed week from a stale snapshot"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 330c1f71-242a-47c7-ac7b-129bd6f5dd3c
  modified: 2026-10-24T14:51:24.467Z
---

The CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts are frozen once per week by the
`/forecast-capture` skill, which snapshots predictions **before kickoff** and reports what
moved since the prior week.

## Scope and entry point (changed 2026-09-02, per Eric)

- **All 16 Big 12 teams every week**, not Baylor only. The list is the `BIG12` constant in
  `weekly_capture.py` — one home; do not copy team lists into the wrapper or the skill.
  `--teams`/`--team` still narrow a run. Budget ~10 min for the full sweep.
- **One entry point:** `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh` (capture → compare
  `--all --archive`). It hardcodes the absolute `uv` path.
- **Archive mirror:** every snapshot and comparison is copied to
  `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`. Read-only copy; truth stays in
  `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. Registered in `backup-manifest.json` as `personal`/ssd —
  see [[backup-sync-system]] for why a new `~/DEV` folder must be added there.
- The ritual guard still keys off the newest `*_baylor.csv`, which the Big 12 sweep always
  writes, so detection is unaffected.

## A gap can mean the other machine captured it

Confirmed 2026-09-09. The Mac's `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` looked like it had
missed 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-31 — it jumped 07-31 → 09-02. Neither week was
missed. **Both were captured on the Windows box**, which runs the same wrapper
against the same repo. The two machines had diverged, each holding captures the
other lacked.

Before declaring a missed week, check the other machine's copy of the log.
Merging is safe: the natural key is `(captured_at, season, team, week, game_id)`,
and a union on that key had **zero conflicts** across 216 Mac + 348 Windows rows
→ 540. Same key never carried different values. See [[github-consolidation]].

**Superseded 2026-10-24:** the capture now runs on the Mac only. The Windows laptop has had no
terminal work or jobs since 2026-10-14 (desktop-app only since 10-21). Check the Windows copy
only for weeks before then; a later gap is a real gap.

## An old newest-snapshot file is not proof of a missed week

Checked 2026-09-02: the newest snapshot was `2026-07-31_baylor.csv`, and both the skill and
COMMANDS.md asserted the 08-24 and 08-31 weeks were "gone for good". They were not — Baylor's
opener was 2026-09-05, so no game had been played and nothing had been overwritten. **A week
is lost only if a game was actually played inside the gap.** Verify before declaring a loss:
